chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who regurgitates from his stomach until it reaches his throat, then he returns it back into his stomach, while he is fasting. He said: 'It is not with anything' (i.e., it does not break the fast).

key_terms.الْقَلْسُ: Regurgitation; bringing food/liquid back up from the stomach to the throat
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ: It is not with anything; a legal idiom meaning it does not invalidate or break the fast

ai.seo_question: Does swallowing regurgitated food break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that regurgitation reaching the throat without being fully expelled does not invalidate the fast, a key distinction in Shia fiqh from complete vomiting. This ruling emphasizes the principle of ease in worship, reflecting the broader jurisprudential consensus that accidental or partial regurgitation is excused. The hadith underscores the importance of intent and physical control in determining the validity of daily rituals.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said

, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who regurgitates from inside him until it reaches his throat, then he returns it back into his inside, and he is Fasting. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man with whose burping something comes up to his throat and then it goes back when he is fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not obligated for anything .’”
